expectations.text: No forced OpenCode dispatch, batch machinery, or unnecessary checkpoints appear in the reply
expectations.evidence: with_skill: 'A one-word spelling fix is trivial, so it takes the smallest applicable path and stays in this parent context. No delegation: it needs no parallelism, context isolation, independent judgment, or specialized capability'; lifecycle collapses PLAN/REVIEW as not triggered; no relay dispatch. old_skill: same conclusion (PLAN skipped, 'trivial, single-line, lower-risk change: no plan artifact, no subagent'), no delegation. Neither forces batch machinery on a one-word fix — the candidate's batch section is correctly conditional, not reflexive.

expectations.text: The reply treats the edit as a small in-parent-context change with a concrete plan to make it
expectations.evidence: with_skill: EXECUTE = 'a single exact-text replacement: only the misspelled word changes' + VALIDATE re-read + no commit; old_skill: EXECUTE = 'Make the minimal edit to the README, that typo only' + validate. Both concrete; both stop before push/merge authority.
